title: Certainty of the indwelling Spirit entails certainty of justification
source_text: X. Deinde quicunque certus est se habere spiritum Dei inhabitantem, dubitare non potest quin sit per veram fidem justificatus, & Deo acceptus. Nec enim spiritus ille datur aliis quam vere credentibus. Sed fideles possunt certo scire se Spiritum Sanctum habere. Nam Apostolus 1 Cor. 2. dicit se & alios fideles Spiritum qui ex Deo est accepisse, ut sciant quae a Deo donata sunt ipsis. Et 1 Joan. 3. In hoc, inquit, scimus quoniam in ipso manemus, & ipse in nobis, quoniam de Spiritu suo dedit nobis. Quod argumentum? Et quomodo ex eo quod spiritum Dei habemus colligere possumus quod in nobis maneat Christus, & nos in ipso.
pass_a_gloss: Next, whoever is certain that he has the indwelling Spirit of God cannot doubt that he is justified by true faith and accepted by God. For that Spirit is not given to any but true believers. But believers can certainly know that they have the Holy Spirit. For the Apostle in 1 Corinthians 2 says that he and other believers have received the Spirit who is from God, that they may know the things freely given them by God. And in 1 John 3: In this we know that we abide in him and he in us, because he has given us of his Spirit. What argument is this? And how from having God’s Spirit can we gather that Christ abides in us and we in him.
pass_b_english: If one knows the Spirit dwells within, one cannot doubt true justifying faith.
Paul and John treat the gift of the Spirit as a known mark of abiding in Christ.
